Decide yourself whether your area is touched (data for a server that serves them to anonymous visitors; texts shown on a page later) and give for each item Q7-Q11 and R3 "met" or "not applicable" with your own check. Own checks to run: the files contain no address, link, email, path, script, markup, control character, invisible or bidi character in any text (search the bytes, not only the visible text), no real person, company, phone or price (the only numbers of 10+ digits are the two invented whatsapp numbers), no secret-like string; the look texts are plain text (REQ-069 security note F-1: every page that shows them must put them as text only); the colours are #rrggbb values from the closed rule; the object ids are from the closed catalogue; serve the folder once (`cd tools && npm run picker -- serve --tenants src/picker/demo-tenants-v3 --port 0 --home <a new folder in the session scratchpad folder named in the launching message>`; stop it afterwards) and ask for a few hostile paths (a path leaving the folder, an unknown tenant, a very long id) over the real HTTP: the answers are the usual 404 and no file of the data folders leaks beyond the questionnaire; the answer files (demo-answers-v3) are not served at all. Findings with severity, file, line, fix. Verdict PASS or FAIL. Change only your handoff. No commits, no git checkout/reset/stash/clean. 16 GB RAM computer: single commands, one server at a time. In your handoff text never list project names or machine paths (say "the traces list").

result.summary:
PASS. Map of surfaces. The change is four new JSON data files (two tenant files of the format /3 in demo-tenants-v3, two answer-set files in demo-answers-v3) and one paragraph in tools/README.md. No code file changed (diff against the tag: only tools/README.md among tracked files; the rest is new files). The surface 'goes to the browser' is touched indirectly: the tenant files are served to anonymous visitors by the picker server (questionnaire and result answers) and their texts are shown by a page later. The surface 'comes from outside' is not touched (no input path changed, the server code is the same). 'writes files', 'holds a secret', 'the server goes by itself', 'photos of people': not touched. 'customer data': the two tenants are invented; the lookup of a tenant is by the id of the path (server code unchanged). tools/README.md: documentation only (surface: none; read for secrets, links, machine paths: none).
Items. Q7 met: byte-level and string-level scan of the four files (about 141 000 byte and code-point probes, 2022 strings and keys, 12 patterns each, own oracle script outside the project) found no secret-like string (no key, token, password words, no long base64 or hex run, no private-key header), the page files (tools/src/picker/public) contain no data of these files, and the questionnaire answers over HTTP hold no rules, points, file names or paths. The only digit runs of 10 or more are the two invented whatsapp numbers (77010000000, 77020000000), published on purpose in leads. Q8 met: each tenant holds no text of the other (counts 0 both ways); the unknown tenant, a tenant-like name that is a data folder, a path with '..', an encoded path and a long id all give one and the same 404 (same hash of the whole answer without the date header); the server takes the tenant from the path only (unchanged code). Q9 not applicable: no query, no database, no string built into a query in the change. Q10 met for the data: both files pass the real check (code 0), the real engine on leader, close and none gives the outcomes of the design over real HTTP, half is refused with a normal answers_invalid answer (not a crash); no new external call. Q11 not applicable: no address that a client sets and the server calls; the files contain no address at all (no scheme, no '//', no www, no domain, no '@'). R3 not applicable (photos of people are not in the product, decision 0033; the change adds none: figures are catalogue ids f01..f08, no image, no data URI). R2 not applicable (Pixel Office untouched).
Own checks of the handoff task. (1) Bytes: all four files are valid UTF-8, no BOM, no control byte except the line feed, no CR, no tab, no DEL, no backslash and no \u escape (so nothing hidden by an escape), no duplicate key, no invisible, bidi, zero-width, variation-selector, private-use, tag or no-break character; the only non-ASCII beyond Cyrillic is the sign of the tenge in price and unit texts. (2) No address, link, email, path, script, markup: patterns for schemes, '//', 'www', domains, '@', slashes and '..', angle brackets, ampersand, backtick, dollar, template braces, 'script', 'on...=', 'javascript', 'url(' : zero hits except the schema value 'sai-picker-tenant/3' (a format name, not a path). (3) No real person, company, phone or price: staff have invented first names only, the operator is marked as an invented firm, the prices are invented text in the design ('from ... tenge' in one solution of each tenant). Platform and product names from the approved sample appear in texts (see finding F1, Low). (4) Look texts are plain text: no markup characters in any text; the pages of the picker site write text only with textContent (search of public/*.js: no innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval; the look section is not yet used by any page file, only by the pure module tenant-look.js), so REQ-069 note F-1 holds for every page that exists now; it stays binding for the pages of REQ-071 and later. (5) Colours: all eight are lower-case #rrggbb. (6) Object ids: all 29 options use ids of the closed catalogue of 15 (shelf, shop, monitor, scanner, tsd, clip, bell, phone, headset, poster, laptop, cell, chart), glyphs from the closed four, figures f01..f08 and shirts from accent, accent2, ink. (7) Real HTTP: the stand was served once on a free port with a new home folder, 39 hostile paths asked (path leaving the folder in plain and encoded form, unknown tenant, a name of a data folder as tenant, 5000-character id and asset name, query with a path and a 5000-character language, null byte, capital letters, double slash, absolute system path, direct file names of both data folders and of answer files): all 404 with the same 118-byte body (one 405 for a GET on the result route, one 200 each for the two pages and the questionnaires), no byte of a data file leaks beyond the questionnaire view, the answer files are not served at all. The server was stopped afterwards (port checked free); the owner's servers were not touched.
